listing.name: annotated — keep the moment
listing.summary: Clip a moment from the page you are on, add your context, and keep the source attached.
listing.description:
Keep the moment before it disappears. Annotated lives in Chrome's side panel, beside the page you are reading. Capture a selected passage, a bounded video or podcast clip, or a snip of the page; add your context; then publish a page that keeps the original source attached.

Core features:
• Capture selected text from the active page, including from the right-click menu.
• Mark a video or podcast range with a server-enforced 90-second maximum.
• Capture a user-drawn snip of the visible page.
• Add a written note or review a recorded audio note before publishing.
• Preserve source links and supported passage or media-time anchors.
• Save bounded draft metadata locally and retry an interrupted capture.
• Follow, respond, and like through Annotated's public reading feed.
• Submit a rights claim from every public annotation page.

How it works:
1. Open a page and select the Annotated toolbar icon.
2. Choose a passage, snip, or media range and add your context.
3. Review the draft, then choose Publish annotation.
4. Open or share the resulting source-backed annotation page.

The Capture surface reads the current tab's URL and title so it can describe the source. It reads selected text or captures a visible snip only for the capture you choose. Nothing is published until you select Publish annotation. See the linked privacy policy for the complete data boundary.
listing.singlePurpose: Capture a user-chosen moment from the current webpage and publish it with personal context and a source link.

dataTypes.scope: Provider account identifier, display name, handle, email when supplied, and avatar URL used for account ownership and attribution.
A short-lived one-time extension ticket and bounded backend session token used to authenticate requested API actions.
Written commentary or recorded audio that the user explicitly chooses to publish.
The current tab URL and title while Capture is open, used to resolve or publish the source; no browsing-history profile is built.
Publish and retry actions needed to complete the user-requested capture.
The selected passage or user-drawn visible-page snip that the user explicitly chooses to publish.

permissionJustifications.sidePanel: Opens Annotated's persistent capture workspace beside the current page.
permissionJustifications.tabs: Reads the active tab URL and title, detects tab changes, and supplies tab context for user-chosen passage and visible-tab capture.
permissionJustifications.scripting: Reads media position and the user's selection while Capture is open, draws the user-requested snip overlay, and highlights a chosen annotation's quoted passage.
permissionJustifications.storage: Stores bounded drafts, API configuration, retry metadata, compact published-result metadata, and the temporary browser session.
permissionJustifications.identity: Completes the configured Google or X server-mediated sign-in handoff and receives its one-time extension callback.
permissionJustifications.alarms: Wakes the service worker to retry queued captures without a persistent background page.
permissionJustifications.contextMenus: Adds one selected-text action that opens the side panel with the user's selection ready to review.
permissionJustifications.favicon: Reads Chrome's local favicon cache so source rows can show their site icon; it does not send favicon data to a remote service.
permissionJustifications.<all_urls>: Lets the persistent Capture surface follow whichever active webpage the user chooses across tab switches and enables visible-tab screenshot capture. Chrome accepts either <all_urls> or a temporary activeTab grant for captureVisibleTab; Annotated does not request activeTab because that grant is tied to one user invocation. While Capture is open, page probes are limited to URL/title, media position, and current selection; snips, highlights, uploads, and publishing require explicit actions.

reviewerInstructions.credentialPlacement: Enter a dedicated reviewer account in the private Test instructions dashboard field only; never commit it to this repository.
steps: Install the uploaded package and confirm the extension ID matches the item ID in the Package tab.
Open a normal HTTPS article, select a short passage, open Annotated, and confirm the Capture surface describes only the active source.
Use the supplied reviewer account to complete either Google or X sign-in and return to the side panel.
Publish the selected passage with a short written note, then open the returned public annotation and its original-source link.
Open a direct video or podcast source, mark a range shorter than 90 seconds, and confirm the panel refuses an over-limit range.
Use the snip control to draw a visible-page region, cancel once to prove nothing uploads, then complete one reviewed snip capture.
Open the public Rights & claims surface and verify a claim can be submitted without exposing dashboard or moderation credentials.
reviewerInstructions.broadHostPermissionNote: Annotated is source-agnostic and its open Capture surface follows the active page across tab switches. It uses <all_urls>, rather than a temporary activeTab grant, for current-page URL/title, media, and selection probes plus user-requested snips or highlights; it does not inject while a feed surface is open, and it never uploads or publishes without an explicit action.
